basis: Cell counts and biomass set how many cells react; per-cell rates come from maintenance power and signalling studies.
equation: C_chem = N_prok × c_cell + N_euk × 2,000 a second, where c_cell = 10 (deep rock) × f_deep + 150 (starved) × f_starved + 5,000 (surface) × f_surface

basis: Prokaryote abundance in soil, ocean, seafloor and deep continental crust, with carbon per cell.
equation: N_cells = B_prok ÷ 25 fg carbon per cell

basis: Counts of the animals that hold most neurons (nematodes, arthropods, vertebrates) and neurons and synapses per animal.
equation: C_nerve = synapses × 0.1 signals per synapse per second

basis: Counts of nematodes, arthropods and vertebrates times neurons per individual.
equation: N_neurons = synapses ÷ 875 synapses per neuron; today checked against animal counts × neurons per animal

basis: Installed computing capacity and the 2026 device inventory with utilisation.
equation: C_silicon = every chip's top speed × share of time busy (60% today); set by hand for earlier moments

basis: Accelerator inventory and utilisation for neural-network workloads.
equation: C_AI = 1.5×10⁷ AI chips (H100-class) × 10¹⁵ operations a second × 60% busy

basis: Neuron counts of the largest brains through time; the largest single machine in the modern inventory.
equation: C_max = the most capable single thinker: the biggest brain's signals a second, or today one 100,000-chip AI cluster

basis: Total DNA in the biosphere, scaled by cell counts at two bits per base pair.
equation: H_DNA = N_prok × 6×10⁶ bits + N_euk × 1.9×10⁸ bits (2 bits per DNA letter)

basis: World capacity to store information outside bodies.
equation: M_outside = installed storage of each era (marks, tablets, books, disks); today 15 zettabytes

basis: Short-lived state per cell and per neuron, plus installed DRAM.
equation: M_active = 100 bits × N_prok + 1,000 × N_euk + 500 × N_neurons + computer memory (DRAM)

basis: Set by hand from the largest known group at each moment (colony, band, city, state, today's 8.1 billion people). No dedicated key source is recorded.
equation: N_group = largest group acting as one (set by hand)

basis: Mass-specific metabolic rates, primary production and maintenance power applied to biomass. Today: 14 TW microbes, 48.5 TW plant, fungal and other complex cells, 2.5 TW animals. Measured top down, plants and algae store about 130 TW as new growth (net primary production), twice this count; the gap is not yet reconciled.
equation: P_bio = P_microbes + P_other cells + P_animals

basis: Set by hand per era (fire, farming, coal, oil). Today's 19.5 TW matches the world's measured primary energy use; 1844 (0.85 TW) and 1890 (1.3 TW, interpolated) follow Our World in Data's world primary energy series (Smil): 0.83 TW in 1840, 0.89 TW in 1850, 1.5 TW around 1905. No source is recorded for other earlier moments.
equation: P_tech = primary energy people use (fire, fuel, electricity), set by hand per era
cite: Energy Institute (2024). Statistical Review of World Energy 2024: world primary energy use 620 EJ in 2023, about 19.6 TW.

basis: Today's 550 Gt carbon is the measured world total; earlier moments are set by hand, moment by moment.
equation: B = B_prok + B_wood + B_euk + B_animal

basis: A model assumption: 85% of microbial DNA and 15% of other DNA is treated as kept by selection. No study measures this share.
equation: H_sel = 0.85 × microbial DNA bits + 0.15 × other DNA bits

basis: Set by hand: DNA counted once per distinct gene family. No source is recorded for this column in the census ledgers.
equation: H_unique = distinct gene families × bits per family (set by hand)

basis: Long-term memory adds three stores: DNA, synapses (4.7 bits each, from spine sizes) and outside memory.
equation: M_kept = H_DNA + 4.7 bits × synapses + M_outside

basis: Animal power scales with animal biomass: 2 Gt carbon of animals today use 2.5 TW. The 2.5 TW is a model assumption.
equation: P_animals = (B_animal ÷ 2 Gt carbon) × 2.5 TW

basis: Total power is life's power plus technology's power.
equation: P = P_bio + P_tech

basis: Electricity used by computers and data centres; today 80 GW from data-centre electricity estimates.
equation: P_computers = electricity used by chips and data centres (set by hand per era)

basis: Electrical signals in plants, fungi and nerveless animals, set by hand. The tree count (S7) gives 3×10²⁰ to 3×10²¹ a second for trees alone; the rest of today's 7×10²³ has no recorded source.
equation: C_electric = cells that signal electrically × signals per cell per second (set by hand)

basis: How far the most capable single thinker sits above a typical cell, in digits.
equation: R = log₁₀(C_max ÷ 1,000 signals a second)

basis: A model assumption: DNA survives as long as its lineage (50 million years for modern lineages). No source is recorded for the lifetimes.
equation: Φ = H_DNA × lineage lifetime in years

basis: Set by hand for each moment, anchored by the model's builder to these temperature reconstructions.
equation: T = global mean surface temperature (set by hand from reconstructions)
cite: Scotese, C. R., Song, H., Mills, B. J. W., & van der Meer, D. G. (2021). Phanerozoic paleotemperatures: the earth's changing climate during the last 540 million years. Earth-Science Reviews, 215, 103503. | Judd, E. J., et al. (2024). A 485-million-year history of Earth's surface temperature. Science, 385, eadk3705.

basis: Set by hand for each moment, anchored by the model's builder to these oxygen reconstructions.
equation: O₂ = share of oxygen in the air (set by hand from reconstructions)
cite: Lyons, T. W., Reinhard, C. T., & Planavsky, N. J. (2014). The rise of oxygen in Earth's early ocean and atmosphere. Nature, 506, 307–315. | Krause, A. J., Mills, B. J. W., Merdith, A. S., Lenton, T. M., & Poulton, S. W. (2022). Extreme variability in atmospheric oxygen levels in the late Precambrian. Science Advances, 8, eabm8191.

basis: Set by hand for each moment, anchored by the model's builder to this CO₂ compilation (about 1,500 estimates from 112 studies).
equation: CO₂ = carbon dioxide in the air, parts per million (set by hand from reconstructions)
cite: Foster, G. L., Royer, D. L., & Lunt, D. J. (2017). Future climate forcing potentially without precedent in the last 420 million years. Nature Communications, 8, 14845.
